title: Cognitive neuroscience
stage: College neuroscience and cognitive science degree
audience: a college student in a neuroscience, cognitive science, psychology or biology degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Learn how mental processes arise from brain activity and how we can tell: the methods (lesions, single neurons, EEG and MEG, functional MRI, brain stimulation) and the logic of inference from each, then attention, perception and object recognition, memory, executive function and the prefrontal cortex, language, emotion and social cognition, decision making, and hemispheric specialization, with the debates about localization, networks and reverse inference.
primary_reading: Neuroscience Online, an open-access textbook from McGovern Medical School at UTHealth Houston (free)

weeks.1: Levels of explanation and the logic of cognitive neuroscience
weeks.5: Functional MRI and the BOLD signal
weeks.6: Brain stimulation: TMS and its logic
weeks.8: Object and face recognition in the ventral stream
weeks.9: Memory systems in the human brain
weeks.10: Executive function and the prefrontal cortex
weeks.11: Language, hemispheres and the split brain
weeks.12: Emotion, social cognition and decision making

blocks.deliverable: Identify single and double dissociations in supplied patient data.
Read an event-related potential experiment and its timing claims.
Evaluate the inferences in a supplied imaging study.
Week 7 midterm; evaluate the evidence for a face-selective region.
Explain a frontal lobe patient's deficits with a cognitive model.
Critique a claim that rests on reverse inference.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Research proposal: write a six-page proposal for a cognitive neuroscience study that tests a specific claim about one cognitive function, with the hypothesis, the method chosen and why the alternatives are weaker, the design and analysis plan, the predicted results, and the alternative explanations your design rules out.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
